provenance.abstraction_rationale: The admitted report describes a segmentation fault in torch.nn.functional.cosine_embedding_loss when called with empty tensors whose input shapes differ, and the resolution patch adds dimension/shape validation. This pattern is scoped to that selected affected API and does not transfer the mechanism to other APIs.
unresolved_information: No explicit root-cause statement was mapped in reported_diagnosis; the mechanism is inferred from the issue comment and resolution patch evidence.

historical_conditions.statement: The reproducer called torch.nn.functional.cosine_embedding_loss with empty tensors: input1 shape [0, 0] and dtype float16, input2 shape [0] and dtype int8, and target shape [0] and dtype float32.
input1 and input2 had different dimensionalities and non-matching shapes, which the documentation does not allow for cosine embedding loss.
The affected implementation did not validate that both input tensors meet the expected dimension/shape constraints before computation.

defect_mechanism.description: The implementation did not enforce equal dimensionality/shape for input1 and input2. Mismatched empty input shapes were allowed to proceed into the computation and resulted in a segmentation fault instead of a controlled RuntimeError.

observed_failure.description: Calling torch.nn.functional.cosine_embedding_loss with empty tensors and mismatched input shapes produced a segmentation fault (core dumped).

historical_observations.statement: The crash was reproduced on the nightly build.
The resolution added tests expecting RuntimeError for differing input shapes/dimensions, including input1 [0,0] with input2 [0] and input1 [1,5] with input2 [1,6].
